# CodeSurf: instructions for coding agents

CodeSurf lets your user ask how something in their code works and explore the answer visually. You investigate the repository and write a small tour file, a JSON list of files, symbols and line numbers. CodeSurf reads the real source, checks every reference, and opens a local viewer in the user's browser. There they can follow the steps, hover for types, click through to definitions, and ask follow-up questions.

Everything runs on the user's computer. The viewer is served from 127.0.0.1:4319.

## Set up (when the user asks you to install or set up CodeSurf)

Run these commands and report what each printed. Stop and tell the user if one fails.

1. Check Node.js. It must be 22.12 or newer:
   node --version
   If it's missing or older, ask the user to install a current Node.js from https://nodejs.org. Don't change their Node installation yourself.

2. Install the CLI:
   npm install -g https://codesurf.io/downloads/codesurf-latest.tgz
   If npm reports a permissions error, tell the user rather than using sudo. They may prefer a Node version manager.
   Optional integrity check: the SHA-256 of the archive is in https://codesurf.io/downloads/latest.json

3. Finish setup:
   codesurf setup
   This links CodeSurf's skill into ~/.claude/skills/codesurf so Claude Code knows the workflow. It also checks for Google Chrome (used for app screenshots) and the Claude Code CLI (used for follow-up questions in the viewer). Tell the user about anything marked ✗; CodeSurf still works without them.

4. If you are not Claude Code (for example Codex, Cursor or Windsurf), suggest that the user add this line to their AGENTS.md or rules file, and add it only if they agree:
   When I ask you to "surf" code or explain code visually, run `codesurf guide` and follow it.

5. Confirm it works:
   codesurf example
   This opens a demo tour in the user's browser. Tell the user it's ready and suggest a first question, for example: "Surf this repo: what happens when a user signs in?"

To update later, re-run step 2. To remove CodeSurf: npm uninstall -g codesurf, then delete ~/.claude/skills/codesurf and ~/.codesurf.

## Use (when the user asks you to "surf" code, or to show or explain how code works)

Run `codesurf guide` and follow it. It prints the complete workflow and the tour format for the installed version. In short:

1. Investigate the real code path that answers the question. Verify each hop in the source.
2. If the flow involves UI, run the app with demo data and capture it with `codesurf shot`, which circles the element that was used.
3. Write tour.json in a scratch directory outside the repository. Put the direct answer in "answer" and the evidence in 3-10 steps. Point at code with paths, symbols and line numbers, plus "text" checks.
4. Run `codesurf open tour.json --repo <repository root>`. Fix any problems it reports by looking at the real lines, then run it again.
5. Reply with the answer in one or two sentences and the URL it printed.

The tour format is also at https://codesurf.io/tour-format.txt
